log.reply:
# Executive Workshop Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Executive Workshop, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0; discovery call notes of 6 October 2026, with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg

Dana Whitfield, thank you for the discovery conversation. This proposal sets out how the Executive Workshop would address the Client's position as recorded in the Profile Block.

## 1. Situation Summary

The Profile Block records the following:

- **Business:** laboratory measurement instruments, design and manufacture; headquartered in the Netherlands; operating in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States.
- **AI use cases:** a customer service chatbot deployed on the support portal; AI visual inspection piloting on the German production line; AI sales forecasting planned for next year.
- **AI maturity:** Piloting.
- **Risk event:** internal audit finding, June 2026: no inventory of AI systems.
- **Regulatory drivers:** EU AI Act; GDPR.
- **Certification target:** ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.
- **Incumbent frameworks:** ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; ISO 9001 quality management system; internal audit function.
- **Constraints:**
  - Budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
  - Customer data must stay in the EU.
  - The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
- **Stated objective (Dana Whitfield):** "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why a One-Day Executive Session Fits

**Maturity.** The Profile Block records the Client's AI maturity as Piloting, with one use case deployed, one piloting and one planned. A single day gives leadership one structured setting to agree intent, principles, sequence and ownership across all three stages. The aim is to reach that agreement before detailed governance work is commissioned.

**Timeline.** The Profile Block records that a decision is expected by 15 December 2026. Two points about that decision are to be confirmed at intake:

- what the decision covers
- whose decision it is

The stated objective sets Q2 2027 as the point by which governance should be in place. The Workshop's draft 12-month roadmap will be sequenced against that objective.

## 3. Four-Block Structure with Client-Specific Emphasis

The day runs as four 90-minute blocks with breaks, using two frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

**Block 1: Alignment**

- The room reviews current AI posture using the three named use cases and the June 2026 internal audit finding.
- The block will define what an AI system inventory should cover across the deployed, piloting and planned use cases.
- Whether any inventory work has begun since June 2026 is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.
- **Output:** a shared statement of governance intent.

**Block 2: Principles**

- The room applies the three Academy principles to each use case: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.
- The block will establish where human accountability sits for each use case. The current human role in visual inspection outcomes is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.
- **Output:** governance operating principles ranked by the room.

**Block 3: Roadmap**

The room sequences governance work against the EU AI Act, GDPR, ISO/IEC 42001 and the incumbent frameworks. AI governance is positioned as an extension of the frameworks the Profile Block names, not a parallel system. Attachment points are as follows:

| Incumbent framework | Attachment point |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS | Unknown, to confirm at intake |
| ISO 9001 quality management system | Unknown, to confirm at intake |
| Internal audit function | Unknown, to confirm at intake |

The roadmap will also carry the stated constraints as sequencing conditions:

- **Works council consultation:** placed as a gate ahead of any step that touches production staff.
- **EU data residency:** placed as a requirement to verify for each use case.

The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done) will frame acceptance criteria for moving visual inspection from pilot to production.

**Output:** a draft 12-month roadmap with owners drawn from the named audience roles.

**Block 4: Decisions**

- The room makes and records decisions on four topics:
  - governance ownership
  - risk appetite for AI
  - oversight cadence
  - budget mandate
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) informs the oversight cadence discussion.
- **Closing slot:** the block closes with *The Turtle and the Phoenix* and the twenty-minute closing exercise from the facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). This slot is the retention device for the three principles.
- **Output:** the decision log.

## 4. Deliverables

1. **Decision log:** decisions taken in Block 4, each with owner, rationale and review date.
2. **Prioritized roadmap:** the draft 12-month roadmap as agreed in the room, with owners.
3. **Readiness observations:** written observations on governance readiness drawn from the workshop record.

Readiness observations are orientation for leadership. They are not an audit opinion and do not predict any ISO/IEC 42001 certification outcome. The delivery date for the written deliverables is to be agreed at intake.

## 5. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** one day, live virtual, four 90-minute blocks with breaks.
- **Audience roles named in the Profile Block:**
  - General Counsel
  - CISO
  - Head of Quality
  - Head of Data
  - German plant manager
  - two internal auditors
- **Optional attendees under the program design:** heads of Legal, Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Information Security.
- **Date:** Unknown, to be set at intake.
- **Price:** US$7,500.

The Profile Block records a budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether that budget covers this engagement is to be confirmed at intake.

## 6. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. What does the decision expected by 15 December 2026 cover, and whose decision is it?
2. Has any AI system inventory work begun since the June 2026 finding?
3. Which ISMS and quality management system artifacts should AI governance attach to?
4. Does the customer service chatbot process customer data, and where is it hosted?
5. Does the visual inspection deployment touch production staff for works council purposes?
6. Is there a target window for the ISO/IEC 42001 start?
7. Which participants will attend, and on what date?

## 7. Regulatory Note

References to the EU AI Act and GDPR in this proposal and in the Workshop are orientation, not legal advice. Two matters require confirmation with external counsel:

- risk classification of each use case under the EU AI Act
- GDPR obligations for each use case

## 8. Next Step

Please reply to confirm a 60-minute intake call. On that call we will resolve the questions in Section 6 and set the Workshop date.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: Item 6 could be scored not applicable because the proposal has no decision items touching regulation. I scored it met because the Regulatory Note carries the external counsel flag. The verdict is the same either way.

'Thank you for the discovery conversation' implies Dana attended the call. SOURCE_MATERIAL lists her among the call participants, so I treated it as traceable. A strict scorer could call it a mild inferred relation.

Statements such as 'Works council consultation: placed as a gate ahead of any step that touches production staff' are consequences of a stated constraint or proposed work, not new Client facts, under the v1.14.3 guidance. A scorer who ignored that guidance might disagree.
The two-page length and the style rules (no em dashes, no Oxford commas) are not checklist items, so I did not score them. I saw no violations on a read-through.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. The proposal restates Profile Block fields, renders unstated relations and artifacts as Unknown or intake questions, and treats the DECISION_TIMELINE as the block states it. It preserves the four-block structure, the program name, duration and price, the exact principles and the framework URLs. It also includes the external counsel flag and the required closing line. No fail indicator appears: there are no invented Client facts, no incumbent register, process, control or record beyond the framework names, and no altered program constants.
